stage: Metadata and identifiability gate; endpoint implementation must be sealed separately before new numeric functional outcomes are extracted
priority_amendment: The latest user instruction prioritizes complete GFP/URA3 synonymous squares and mitochondrial structure-to-function. The constant-CDS bacterial UTR decay route is deferred. Earlier gates, failed predictions and adaptive choices remain recorded.
known_information: Published negative epistasis and mitochondrial remodeling conclusions have been read; this is a retrospective public-data reanalysis.
The 2026 S7 workbook has 4068 single and 46622 double labels, no triple labels, and ten gene/promoter/medium columns. Fitness values have not been extracted.

Current GFP methods pool replicate genotype frequencies and discard fitness below 0.5. The archived S7 has no explicit replicate or standard-error columns. WT normalization and the earlier study must be verified.

The Science structural study has two WT and two LRPPRC-KO DMS samples. Its directly reported translation ratio has three assays for ATP8/ATP6, not eleven independent transcript outcomes. Soto et al. 2022 is an unresolved functional-data lead.

A.eligibility: Require an author-verified full reporter CDS and coordinate convention; WT/single1/single2/double with identical translated proteins; all four measurements in exactly one gene/promoter/medium. A wild-type value fixed by normalization is a reference, not an independent replicate.
A.identifiability: A complete two-site square has one residual degree of freedom beyond an intercept and two main effects. Its log-scale contrast does not alone reject a global nonlinear transformation of additive latent effects. Reciprocal sign epistasis or a strict two-peak accessibility obstruction cannot be generated by a monotone transformation of an additive two-site field. Nonmonotone global responses remain an alternative.
A.endpoint_plan: Primary endpoint is the complete-square log-fitness interaction and a scale-robust reciprocal-sign/accessibility diagnostic, subject to documented positive relative-fitness semantics. Freeze a single primary condition using assay design and coverage only. Other conditions are sensitivity analyses.
baselines: Additive log-relative-fitness effects from the two singles
Monotone global-nonlinearity model trained without held-out double outcomes
Simple position, nucleotide, GC and codon features when enough independent groups exist
A.dependence: Report unique single mutants, doubles, codon pairs and reporters. Split or cluster by connected components of squares sharing a mutant where possible. A two-reporter analysis cannot establish broad gene generalization. Never count conditions as biological replicates.
A.validation: Before reading numeric outcomes, preserve a metadata-defined set of doubles where usable and seal all rules. If dependency components or unavailable replicate data prevent credible validation, label analysis descriptive; do not invent standard errors or use mutant resampling as measurement uncertainty.
A.failure: No verified CDS or no complete synonymous squares means an eligibility failure. No recoverable replicate/count uncertainty limits interaction significance. A nonzero contrast compatible with global nonlinearity does not establish local mechanistic interaction. Censoring below 0.5 bounds accessibility and must not be treated as random missingness.
A.budget: Processed tables and code inspection first; no raw-read pipeline, exhaustive folding or new reporter design in this pilot.

B.eligibility: Verify source/reference coordinates by sequence alignment, cell background, perturbation, structural samples, RNA abundance and translation provenance. Same line and perturbation in a separate publication are cross-study compatible, not same-sample matched.
B.identifiability: At most eleven mitochondrial transcript/bicistronic units. An ensemble comparison needs transcript-resolved paired functional measurements, not one ATP8/ATP6 ratio or WT-only ribosome density. Distinguish fitted probing summaries from independently predicted function.
B.endpoint_plan: Primary response is log KO/WT measured translation with log KO/WT RNA abundance as a covariate; if only metabolic labeling is available call it synthesis signal, not ribosome occupancy or translation efficiency. No response is defined by subtraction of incompatible assays.
baselines: Abundance plus one prespecified simple DMS/initiation summary
The same baseline plus one experimentally informed ensemble feature
B.validation: Leave transcript/bicistronic unit out, with features and any tunable ensemble parameters fitted inside the training fold. Use at most one added ensemble feature in the bounded pilot. Report every held-out error and all eleven-or-fewer independent units; no window-level pseudoreplication.
B.failure: Absent compatible RNA/translation measurements is a data-information failure. Too few complete independent units to compare baselines is a design failure. A nonimproving held-out ensemble feature is a failed predictive hypothesis within the tested conditions. No new biological variant effects are inferred.
B.budget: Small source and processed-data recovery plus coordinate audit first. No large ensemble optimization or raw sequencing reanalysis before functional-data closure.

selection: Choose expansion by construct/assay validity, usable independent units, ability to reject competing explanations and incremental validation evidence. A positive result is not required. Preserve untouched outcomes if either gate fails.
claim_scope: Measured function, structural occupancy, logical compatibility and folding-model accessibility are separate levels. Only evidence at its measured level can close the immediate milestone.
